question.text: Let $C = \{-3, -1, 1, 3\}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to $\mathbf{1}_C(-1)?$
question.explanation:
The indicator function $\mathbf{1}[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false. \[ \mathbf{1}[P] = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if $P$ is true}, \\[3pt] 0, & \text{if $P$ is false}. \end{cases} \]

Recall that the indicator function $\mathbf{1}_C(x)$ of a set $C$ equals $1$ if $x \in C$ and $0$ if $x \notin C.$ This can be written using Iverson bracket notation as \[ \mathbf{1}_C(x) = \mathbf{1}[x \in C]. \]

Therefore, we have \[ \mathbf{1}_C(-1) = \mathbf{1}[-1 \in C] = \mathbf{1}[-1 \in \{-3, -1, 1, 3\}]. \]

question.text: Let $D = \{0, 5, 10\}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to $\mathbf{1}_D(7)?$
question.explanation:
The indicator function $\mathbf{1}[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false. \[ \mathbf{1}[P] = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if $P$ is true}, \\[3pt] 0, & \text{if $P$ is false}. \end{cases} \]

Recall that the indicator function $\mathbf{1}_D(x)$ of a set $D$ equals $1$ if $x \in D$ and $0$ if $x \notin D.$ This can be written using Iverson bracket notation as \[ \mathbf{1}_D(x) = \mathbf{1}[x \in D]. \]

Therefore, we have \[ \mathbf{1}_D(7) = \mathbf{1}[7 \in D] = \mathbf{1}[7 \in \{0, 5, 10\}]. \]

The indicator function $\mathbf{1}[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false. \[ \mathbf{1}[P] = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if $P$ is true}, \\[3pt] 0, & \text{if $P$ is false}. \end{cases} \]

The expression $\mathbf{1}[x_i > 0] \cdot x_i$ equals $x_i$ when $x_i > 0$ and equals $0$ otherwise. Thus, the sum \[ \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{5} \mathbf{1}[x_i > 0] \cdot x_i \] adds up only the positive values.

We evaluate the indicator function for each $x_i{:}$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_1 > 0] = \mathbf{1}[9 > 0] = 1$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_2 > 0] = \mathbf{1}[-8 > 0] = 0$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_3 > 0] = \mathbf{1}[-1 > 0] = 0$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_4 > 0] = \mathbf{1}[4 > 0] = 1$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_5 > 0] = \mathbf{1}[2 > 0] = 1$

Therefore, \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^{5} \mathbf{1}[x_i > 0] \cdot x_i &= 1 \cdot 9 + 0 \cdot (-8) + 0 \cdot (-1) + 1 \cdot 4 + 1 \cdot 2 \\ &= 9 + 0 + 0 + 4 + 2 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{15}. \end{align*}

question.explanation:
The indicator function $\mathbf{1}[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false. \[ \mathbf{1}[P] = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if $P$ is true}, \\[3pt] 0, & \text{if $P$ is false}. \end{cases} \]

The expression $\mathbf{1}[x_i \ge 0] \cdot (2x_i) + \mathbf{1}[x_i < 0] \cdot 1$ equals $2x_i$ when $x_i \ge 0$ and equals $1$ when $x_i < 0.$ Thus, the sum \[ \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{5} \mathbf{1}[x_i \ge 0] \cdot (2x_i) + \mathbf{1}[x_i < 0] \cdot 1 \] adds $2x_i$ for nonnegative values and $1$ for negative values.

We evaluate the indicator function for each $x_i{:}$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_1 \ge 0] = \mathbf{1}[-6 \ge 0] = 0,$ $\mathbf{1}[x_1 < 0] = 1$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_2 \ge 0] = \mathbf{1}[-1 \ge 0] = 0,$ $\mathbf{1}[x_2 < 0] = 1$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_3 \ge 0] = \mathbf{1}[0 \ge 0] = 1,$ $\mathbf{1}[x_3 < 0] = 0$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_4 \ge 0] = \mathbf{1}[4 \ge 0] = 1,$ $\mathbf{1}[x_4 < 0] = 0$

  • $\mathbf{1}[x_5 \ge 0] = \mathbf{1}[7 \ge 0] = 1,$ $\mathbf{1}[x_5 < 0] = 0$

Therefore, \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^{5} \mathbf{1}[x_i \ge 0] \cdot (2x_i) + \mathbf{1}[x_i < 0] \cdot 1 &= 1 + 1 + 2 \cdot 0 + 2 \cdot 4 + 2 \cdot 7 \\ &= 1 + 1 + 0 + 8 + 14 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{24}. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $B = \{2, 4, 6, 8\}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to $\mathbf{1}[5 \in B]?$
question.explanation:
The indicator function $\mathbf{1}[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false. \[ \mathbf{1}[P] = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if $P$ is true}, \\[3pt] 0, & \text{if $P$ is false}. \end{cases} \]

Recall that the indicator function $\mathbf{1}_A(x)$ of a set $A$ equals $1$ if $x \in A$ and $0$ if $x \notin A.$ This can be written using Iverson bracket notation as \[ \mathbf{1}_A(x) = \mathbf{1}[x \in A]. \]

Here, the Iverson bracket expression $\mathbf{1}[5 \in B]$ has $x = 5$ and $A = B.$ Therefore, converting back to set indicator notation, we have \[ \mathbf{1}[5 \in B] = \mathbf{1}_B(5). \]
